args.message: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-banker-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though the docstring already said ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

This PR changes `round_money` to quantize with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, which matches FIN-212 and the existing tests.

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

args.body:
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though the docstring already said ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

This PR changes `round_money` to quantize with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, which matches FIN-212 and the existing tests.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug and opened PR #101 against main, with review requested from alex. CI passed on the latest version of the branch.

- **The bug:** `src/money.py` was rounding with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its own comment says it should use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (FIN-212). Because of that, `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` gave 2.67 instead of the 2.66 the test expects.
- **The fix:** on a new branch, `fix/money-banker-rounding`, I changed the import and the `quantize` call to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Nothing else changed.
- **CI:** the first run passed (ci-0001), but the pull request was blocked because main had moved ahead of the branch. I merged main into the branch, checked that the fix was still there, and ran CI again (ci-0002, commit 0a9452f727). That run passed too, and then I opened the PR: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

I didn't merge the PR, because merging into main needs a code owner's approval. I also couldn't find FIN-212 in the advisory lookup, so I went by the comment in the code and the test.
